title: Around town: autos, cabs & the metro
goal: Get an auto to go by the meter, tell a driver where to turn and stop, book a cab or a bike taxi, ask how long a trip takes and survive the Mumbai local and the metro.
intro:
Pune and Mumbai run on autos, app cabs, bike taxis, the metro and — in Mumbai — the famous **local** trains. This unit gives you the lines you need every day: **कोथरूडला येणार का?**, **मीटर टाका**, **पुढच्या सिग्नलवरून डावीकडे घ्या**, **इथेच थांबवा**, and on a packed train, **उतरणार का?**

The grammar is the grammar of getting things done: driver instructions with **घ्या, थांबवा, सोडा**, Marathi's **compound verbs** (बुक करून **टाक** 'just book it', तिकीट काढून **घे** 'get yourself a ticket', सोडून **दे** 'drop me'), and **लागणे** for how long or how much a trip takes.

grammar.title: Telling the driver, and compound verbs: करून टाक, काढून घे, सोडून दे
grammar.body:
**Directing a driver.** Use the polite **-आ** form, even to an auto driver: **घ्या** 'take (a turn)': डावीकडे घ्या, यू-टर्न घ्या, **पुढे घ्या** 'go on a bit', **बाजूला घ्या** 'pull over'; **थांबवा** 'stop (the vehicle)'; **सोडा** 'drop (me)': मला इथे सोडा. **थांबवा** is the causative of थांबणे — 'make it stop'. Plain **थांबा** also works, but it really means 'wait'.

**Compound verbs.** Marathi often puts the main verb in the **-ऊन** form and adds a second, 'helper' verb that colours the action:

**-ऊन टाकणे** — get it done, just do it (completely): कॅब बुक **करून टाक** 'just book a cab'; पैसे **देऊन टाक** 'just pay (and be done)'.
**-ऊन घेणे** — do it for yourself: तिकीट **काढून घे** 'get yourself a ticket'; नीट **बघून घ्या** 'check properly (for your own good)'.
**-ऊन देणे** — do it for someone else: मला **सोडून दे** 'drop me (do me that favour)'.

Only the helper verb changes for person and tense: करून टाकतो, करून टाकलं.

The trap: the helper verbs lose their own meaning here. **काढून घे** isn't 'take out and take', and **सोडून दे** can also mean 'give up, forget about it' — context decides.

examples.en: Please drop me at the metro station.

grammar.title: It takes (time, money): लागणे
grammar.body:
English 'it takes an hour' is **लागणे** in Marathi. The **time or money is the subject**, and the person, if mentioned, takes **-ला**:

**मला** अर्धा तास **लागला** 'it took me half an hour' (lit. 'to me half an hour was needed').

So लागणे agrees with the time: **एक तास लागतो** (m sg), **दोन तास लागतात** (pl), **वीस मिनिटं लागतात** (n pl), **खूप वेळ लागला**. Future: **लागेल** (one thing) / **लागतील** (several): किती वेळ लागेल? · किती पैसे लागतील?

**For doing something**: verb + **-आयला**: इथे **यायला** दोन तास लागले 'it took two hours to get here'.

**From… to…**: X**-हून** / X**-पासून** … Y**-ला** / Y**-पर्यंत**: पुण्याहून मुंबईला. **About**: **जवळपास** or **साधारण**. **How far**: किती लांब आहे? / अंतर किती आहे?

The trap: don't translate 'take' with घेणे. *मी अर्धा तास घेतला* is wrong; say **मला अर्धा तास लागला**.

examples.native: पुण्याहून मुंबईला जवळपास तीन तास लागतात.
examples.roman: puṇyāhūn mumbaīlā dzavaḷpās tīn tās lāgtāt.
examples.en: It takes about three hours from Pune to Mumbai.
By metro it'll take twenty minutes.

examples.native: मला ऑफिसला पोहोचायला एक तास लागला.
examples.roman: malā ôfislā pohotsāylā ek tās lāglā.
examples.en: It took me an hour to get to the office.
How much will an auto cost?

dialogue.title: An auto to Kothrud
dialogue.setting: Pune, outside Pune railway station in the evening rush. Meera, a student, stops an auto.

lines.speaker: Meera
lines.native: तीनशे? खूप जास्त सांगताय! मीटर टाका ना.
lines.roman: tīnshe? khūp dzāst sāṅgtāy! mīṭar ṭākā nā.
lines.en: Three hundred? That's way too much! Put the meter on, please.

lines.speaker: Driver
lines.native: या वेळी ट्रॅफिक असतं, ताई. बरं, बसा, मीटरने चलतो.
lines.roman: yā veḷī ṭræfik astaṃ, tāī. baraṃ, basā, mīṭarne tsalto.
lines.en: There's traffic at this time, miss. OK, get in, I'll go by the meter.

lines.speaker: Driver
lines.native: जवळपास अर्धा तास. कर्वे रोडने जाऊ का?
lines.roman: dzavaḷpās ardhā tās. karve roḍne dzāū kā?
lines.en: About half an hour. Shall I go by Karve Road?

lines.speaker: Meera
lines.native: हो, चालेल. काका, पुढच्या सिग्नलवरून उजवीकडे घ्या.
lines.roman: ho, tsālel. kākā, puḍhchyā signalvarūn udzvīkaḍe ghyā.
lines.en: Yes, fine. (later) Uncle, turn right at the next signal.

lines.speaker: Driver
lines.native: इथे? पण इथे नो एंट्री आहे.
lines.roman: ithe? paṇ ithe no enṭrī āhe.
lines.en: Here? But it's no entry here.

lines.speaker: Meera
lines.native: अरे हो! मग पुढे यू-टर्न घ्या आणि पहिल्या गल्लीत वळा.
lines.roman: are ho! mag puḍhe yū-ṭarn ghyā āṇi pahilyā gallīt vaḷā.
lines.en: Oh yes! Then take a U-turn up ahead and turn into the first lane.

lines.speaker: Meera
lines.native: बस, बस, इथेच थांबवा. किती झाले?
lines.roman: bas, bas, ithets thāmbavā. kitī dzhāle?
lines.en: That's it, stop right here. How much is it?

lines.speaker: Meera
lines.native: हे घ्या दोनशे. सुटे वीस आहेत का?
lines.roman: he ghyā donshe. suṭe vīs āhet kā?
lines.en: Here, two hundred. Have you got twenty change?

lines.speaker: Driver
lines.en: Yes, here you go. Take care.

culture: Pune auto drivers are notorious for quoting a flat price or refusing short trips, so **मीटर टाका** and **मीटरने चला** are worth practising; at night (midnight to 5 am) a higher night fare is legal. People call drivers **दादा** or **भाऊ**, and in Pune often **काका** or even **मामा**; drivers call young women **ताई** and older people **काका / मावशी**. In Mumbai, autos don't run in the south of the city — there you take the black-and-yellow **काळी-पिवळी** taxis or a cab. App cabs and bike taxis (Ola, Uber, Rapido) are everywhere; the driver will call and ask **कुठे आहात?** and then **ओटीपी सांगा**. The Mumbai **local** is its own world: know whether your train is **फास्ट** or **स्लो**, which line (वेस्टर्न, सेंट्रल, हार्बर) you're on, and that women have their own **लेडीज डबा**. Before your station, ask the person ahead **उतरणार का?** and swap places — standing at the door when you're not getting off earns you a loud **आत चला!** Pune and Mumbai both now have metro lines, which are clean, air-conditioned and much calmer.

tip.title: Getting an auto to go
tip.body:
- Ask **X-ला येणार का? / चलणार का?** 'will you go to X?' — the place takes **-ला**.
- Insist on the meter: **मीटर टाका**, **मीटरने चला**.
- Use the polite **-आ** form with drivers (टाका, चला, थांबवा) and call them **दादा, भाऊ** or **काका**.
- Too much? **खूप जास्त सांगताय!**

sentences.native: फक्त तीन किलोमीटर आहे, दीडशे खूप जास्त आहेत.

sentences.roman: mīṭarne tsalā, nāhītar mī dusrī rikṣā ghete.

Will you go to Kothrud?

In Mumbai auto drivers always go by the meter.

lessons.title: Telling the driver where to go

tip.title: घ्या, थांबवा, सोडा
tip.body:
- Turn: **डावीकडे / उजवीकडे घ्या**, **यू-टर्न घ्या**, **पुढे घ्या** 'go on a bit'.
- Stop: **थांबवा** 'stop (the vehicle)' — the causative of थांबणे.
- Drop: **मला इथे सोडा**.
- 'At the signal / corner': **सिग्नलवरून**, **कोपऱ्यावर**.
tip.pattern: डावीकडे घ्या · इथेच थांबवा · मला इथे सोडा

sentences.en: Stop at the next corner.
Turn left into the second lane.

sentences.en: The mall's across the road, you'll have to take a U-turn.

lessons.title: Booking a cab or a bike

tip.title: करून टाक, बघून घे, सोडून दे
tip.body:
- Add a helper verb to the **-ऊन** form: **करून टाक** 'just do it', **बघून घे** 'check it (for yourself)', **सोडून दे** 'drop me (for me)'.
- Only the helper changes: करून टाकतो, करून टाकलं.
- App words take **करणे**: कॅब **बुक कर**, **ओटीपी सांग**.

sentences.native: कॅब बुक करून टाक, उशीर होतोय.
sentences.roman: kæb buk karūn ṭāk, ushīr hotoy.
sentences.en: Just book a cab, we're getting late.
A bike taxi works out cheaper on the app.
Did you give the driver the OTP?
The driver cancelled the cab!

sentences.native: सामान नीट बघून घ्या, काही विसरू नका.
sentences.roman: sāmān nīṭ baghūn ghyā, kāhī visarū nakā.
sentences.en: Check your things properly, don't forget anything.

sentences.native: ड्रायव्हर म्हणतोय की तो पाच मिनिटांत पोहोचतो.
sentences.roman: ḍrāyvhar mhaṇtoy kī to pāts miniṭānt pohotsto.
sentences.en: The driver says he'll be here in five minutes.

sentences.native: मी बाईक बुक करते, कॅबपेक्षा लवकर पोहोचेन.
sentences.roman: mī bāīk buk karte, kæbpekṣā lavkar pohotsen.
sentences.en: I'll book a bike, I'll get there quicker than by cab. (woman)

sentences.native: कॅब बुक करू का, की रिक्षा घेऊया?
sentences.roman: kæb buk karū kā, kī rikṣā gheūyā?
sentences.en: Shall I book a cab, or shall we get an auto?

sentences.native: हे पैसे ठेवून घ्या, सुटे नकोत.
sentences.roman: he paise ṭhevūn ghyā, suṭe nakot.
sentences.en: Keep the money, no change needed.
Drop me at the station, will you? (to a friend)

tip.title: लागणे — it takes
tip.body:
- The time is the subject: **एक तास लागतो**, **दहा मिनिटं लागतात**; the person takes -ला: **मला** दोन तास **लागले**.
- Future: **लागेल** (one) / **लागतील** (several).
- 'To do it': **-आयला**: इथे **यायला** किती वेळ लागतो?
- Never घेणे for 'take time'.

sentences.en: By bus it takes about an hour.
It's a ten-minute walk.

sentences.native: मला इथे यायला दोन तास लागले!

sentences.en: It took me two hours to get here!

lessons.title: On the local and the metro

tip.title: Catching trains: पकडणे, चुकणे, उतरणे
tip.body:
- **लोकल पकडली** 'I caught the local' — but **लोकल चुकली** 'I missed the local' (the train is the subject).
- **फास्ट** trains skip stations, **स्लो** ones stop everywhere.
- Before your stop, ask **उतरणार का?** 'getting off?'.
- In a crush you'll hear **आत चला!** 'move in!'

sentences.native: मी आठ वाजताची फास्ट लोकल पकडली.
sentences.roman: mī āṭh vādztātsī fāsṭ lokal pakaḍlī.
sentences.en: I caught the eight o’clock fast local.

sentences.native: लोकल चुकली, पुढची पाच मिनिटांनी आहे.

sentences.en: Missed the local — the next one is in five minutes.

The last compartment is less crowded.
Which metro line goes to the airport?

sentences.en: Come by metro, you'll get here quicker than by bus.
